steps.body: Converting length runs both ways: meters to centimeters multiplies by 100, and centimeters to meters divides by it.
steps.narration: Converting length runs both ways: meters to centimeters multiplies by 100, and centimeters to meters divides by it.

widget.prompt: How many centimeters in 4 meters? Hop one meter at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Three hops reach 300 cm; the object is four meters long.
Five hops overshoot — four meters is 400 centimeters.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 430, 3 hops land on 460.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — four meters needs four hops of 100 centimeters.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — four meters stops exactly at 400 centimeters.

predict.prompt: 500 cm in meters — will the number grow or shrink?
predict.reveal: Meters are bigger, so fewer of them cover the same rope: 500 cm is only 5 m.

cml.actionGoal: Hold the quantity fixed while the unit changes, and watch which way the NUMBER moves for g4v length.
invariants: Converting never changes how much there is: a smaller unit needs more of them and a bigger unit needs fewer, so the number moves in the opposite direction to the unit size in g4v length.
misconceptions: Multiplying when converting to a bigger unit, adding the conversion factor instead of multiplying by it, or comparing bare numbers across different units.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A route measures 7 kilometers, and each kilometer is 1000 meters. Compute 7 × 1000.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding mixes a quantity with a rate. Each of the 7 kilometers contributes 1000 meters, so they multiply.
That divided. Going to the SMALLER unit needs more of them, so the number must grow.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.

widget.prompt: Converting 5 kilograms into grams, do you multiply or divide by 1,000?

options.label: Multiply — grams are smaller, so there are more of them
options.feedback: Correct — each kilogram contains 1,000 grams, so 5 kilograms is 5,000 grams.

options.label: Divide — the number should get smaller
options.feedback: Dividing would give 0.005, which is far less than the mass you started with.

options.label: Neither — the number stays the same
options.feedback: The mass stays the same, but the NUMBER must change because the unit changed.

options.label: Multiply by 100
options.feedback: 100 is the centimeters-per-meter factor; a kilogram holds 1,000 grams.
